# gitmoap_catalog_service_deployments (Data Source)

A service's deployment history. Every deployment of the service, newest first: the environment, the repository and commit, the pipeline run that performed it, and its status. Deployments are recorded by the platform as pipelines run, never written through the API; a rollback is a new deployment that supersedes the previous one. Filter by `environment_id` or `status`; pages hold up to 100 (20 by default). Reporters and above may call it: deployments are not public, even on a public group.

The token needs `catalog:read`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `service_id` (String) The service's id

### Optional

- `environment_id` (String) Only deployments to this environment
- `status` (String) Filter by deployment status

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `approved_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--approved_by))
- `attempt` (Number)
- `commit_sha` (String)
- `deployment_id` (String)
- `environment_id` (String)
- `error_summary` (String)
- `finished_at` (String)
- `node_id` (String)
- `pipeline_run_id` (String)
- `ref_name` (String)
- `repository_id` (String)
- `service_id` (String)
- `started_at` (String)
- `status` (String) Where a deployment is in its life. It starts `requested`; waits as `awaiting_approval` when the
environment needs approval, ending `rejected` if refused; then `running`, ending `succeeded`,
`failed` or `cancelled`. `skipped` means another deploy held the environment and its policy is to
skip. A successful deployment becomes `superseded` when a later one replaces it.
- `triggered_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--triggered_by))

<a id="nestedatt--items--approved_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.approved_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
